subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up & confirmation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about Sunnyside's ingestion use case and the downstream workflows where you do entity extraction and care-team routing. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the immediate items we discussed and get confirmation on a couple of PII-specific points so I can pull in Security/Platform if needed.

Recap / asks:
- Use case: clinical intake forms -> LLM extract -> EHR mapping. Sensitive PHI/PII in prompts/outputs.
- Primary requirement: no prompts/outputs used for model training; stricter log retention and residency controls required.
- Questions for your team (please confirm):
  1) Do you need Redwood-hosted inference (hosted API) or would Dedicated/Private be required based on residency/non-storage needs?
  2) Required data residency region (US / EU / other)?
  3) Minimum retention requirement for logs/audit traces (e.g., 0 days, 30 days, 90 days)?

What I can confirm today (high level):
- By default, Redwood-hosted retains request/response content for up to 30 days to support debugging and incident investigations.
- We do not surface customer prompts/outputs to model training pipelines unless explicitly agreed and contracted (we can provide this in writing).
- Enterprise Dedicated/Private options allow you to configure retention and disable hosted logging — we can set retention to 0 and disable diagnostic storage when running in Private mode.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm answers to the 3 items above?
- I attached a draft mutual action plan and our standard security questionnaire — once you confirm residency/retention we can schedule a 30-min call with Neha (security) to run through specifics.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, security-questionnaire.pdf

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: production data must be stored and processed in the US (us-west preferred).
- Retention: we need the option to retain zero copies of prompts/outputs in your hosted environment — if hosted can't support 0 retention, we will require Dedicated or Private.
- PHI/PII fields: names, DOB, SSN equivalents, free-text clinical notes. We will provide a sample schema.

Specific questions:
1) On the hosted plan, you mentioned 30 days by default. Is that configurable per-customer?
2) How are logs/requests encrypted in transit and at rest? Is KMS/HSM integration available for tenant keys?
3) You said prompts/outputs are not used for training by default — can you confirm that is both a policy and a technical safeguard (i.e., no dataset ingestion)?

I'm attaching our internal security requirements doc — if you could have Neha confirm the answers we can move to the MAP and a short security call next week.

Thanks,
Alex Jensen
Head of Data Integrations
Sunnyside Health
alex.jensen@sunnysidehealth.com

Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up & next steps

Alex — looping Neha in to confirm the security details below. Short answers up front, then Neha added a couple more notes.

Short answers (Redwood-hosted default):
- Retention: default request/response content retention is 30 days (configurable on Enterprise tiers).
- Configuration: Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention to 0 and disable persistent diagnostic storage.
- Training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/outputs to train models by default. Any use for training would require a separate, opt-in agreement and explicit contracts (we will not do this without customer consent).
- Encryption: TLS for transit; at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS available on Private deployments and via BYOK on Enterprise Dedicated (we can provide KMS integration details).

Neha (Security) — additional details and an excerpt you can share with your InfoSec team:
- Hosted logs/audit traces: metadata (request timestamps, model used, latency) is retained longer for billing/analytics; full prompt + full output content stored encrypted for up to 30 days by default.
- Caching: Redwood may cache inference results (prefix / KV cache) to improve latency; cache keys are scoped per-customer and TTLs are short (by default up to 7 days) — cache can be disabled for Dedicated/Private.
- Access controls: only authorized ops/security engineers have access to decrypted request/response content for incident response — all access is audited.
- Data residency: Hosted offers region selection; however, for strict residency +/- zero retention, Private or Dedicated is recommended.

Attachments: pii-handling-summary.pdf

Next steps:
- If Sunnyside can accept the hosted default for evaluation, we can proceed with the MAP and a 30-day eval with stricter RBAC.
- If you need 0 retention or US-only processing for production, let's scope Dedicated/Private — I can have Marissa run an initial sizing & estimate.
- I'll attach a one-page excerpt you can share with InfoSec (pii-handling-summary.pdf) and propose a 30-min call with Neha next Tue/Thu.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks — that helps. Two quick clarifications before we schedule the security call: 
1) Can you confirm whether token-level logs (i.e., tokenized prompt/output) are stored or just the raw text?
2) Will any of the prompt/output content be used in aggregated telemetry or model improvement pipelines in anonymized form without an explicit contract?

If you can confirm both as no (tokens not stored separately; no training telemetry without opt-in) I think we're comfortable moving forward with the eval and MAP.

Alex

Alex — short confirmations inline:
1) Token-level logs: we do not store separate tokenized logs as a distinct artifact. Stored request/response content is the raw prompt and raw model output (encrypted at rest). Tokenization is part of the runtime pipeline but we do not persist a token stream as a separate log.
2) Aggregated telemetry / model improvement: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/outputs for model training or improvement unless explicitly contracted and consented to. We will provide that as contractual language in the DPA and Master Services Agreement.

Confirming next steps:
- I'll send an updated MAP and proposed security call times (Neha: Tue/Thu next week).
- Marissa will follow up with a Dedicated sizing if you decide 0 retention/US-only production is required.

If you want a single written confirmation for your InfoSec team, we can issue a short statement: "Redwood will not use customer prompts/outputs for model training without explicit opt-in; hosted default retention for full prompt/output content is 30 days; Dedicated/Private options support configurable/zero retention and customer-managed KMS." I can get this signed by legal on request.

Thanks,
